subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the force on a conductor of length l carrying a current i when it is situated in a magnetic field of induction B? When is it maximum?

mark_split.label: F = B i l sin θ

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: F = Bil sin θ with θ the angle between the conductor and the field; maximum F = Bil at θ = 90°; as a vector F = i(l × B). Matches the book's answer.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: Write the sin θ form first — the maximum mark is only earned by naming θ = 90° and dropping sin θ to 1.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Saying what θ is counts as part of the formula.
steps.why: Only the part of the field at right angles to the current pushes on the conductor — that is what sin θ measures.
common_mistakes: Writing F = B i l and forgetting sin θ.
Taking θ as the angle with the normal. Here θ is between the conductor and the field.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give the condition (θ = 90°) and the value (B i l) together.
steps.why: sin θ is largest at θ = 90°, so the same current in the same field pushes hardest when the conductor lies at right angles to the field.
common_mistakes: Saying maximum when the conductor is parallel to the field. Parallel gives θ = 0° and zero force.
Giving the condition without the maximum value B i l.

recall.must_convey: That the force is maximum at θ = 90°, where F = B i l.
accept: F max is B i l

steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular pushes most, parallel pushes nothing: sin 90° = 1, sin 0° = 0.
